title: LastBuy: every unit justified before the final order
description: LastBuy helps an industrial thermal-camera manufacturer decide its final purchase of a discontinued processor while protecting contracted repair coverage. In a constructed enterprise case, reconciling component coverage, usable stock, duplicate custody and confirmed inbound changes an 18,000-unit, $1.44 million proposal into a 10,000-unit, $800,000 recommendation. The $640,000 difference is modeled, not achieved savings. Four scoped Microsoft Foundry roles quote engineering, service, supply and supplier evidence; deterministic code checks quantities and source freshness. A captured Foundry response summarized 4,800 current units correctly but supplied an older 6,000-unit value in a structured field. Current validation blocks approval and export until the stock record is corrected and analysis rerun. The workflow requires separate engineering, service, finance and procurement approvals of the same plan version; the cloud tenant currently has only a planner user. Export recovery was tested against an ERP simulation. A customer pilot will measure planning time, service coverage and finance-reviewed outcomes.

beats.screen: Completed enterprise case: $1.44m proposal, 18,000 units, service supply-chain buyer
beats.action: Open LTB-CLOUD-RELEASE-7 at Decision overview. Point to the original proposal; leave the example/recorded-results label visible.
beats.narration: One final order. Years of service obligations. How many chips should you buy? LastBuy helps a thermal-camera manufacturer's service supply-chain director decide. This example starts at 1.44 million dollars. The business records are examples; these are completed Foundry results.

beats.screen: Governing service evidence: processor coverage and 22,000 protected demand
beats.action: Evidence → SERVICE-SYN-A07 → Inspect. Hold on processor coverage and the increase to 22,000. Close and return to Decision overview.
beats.narration: First, inspect what we must protect. In this constructed case, a signed service amendment covers the processor and raises protected demand to twenty-two thousand units. A detector warranty alone cannot establish that obligation. Engineering checks released compatibility; service identifies the governing coverage. Buying less is acceptable only if service coverage survives.

beats.screen: Quantity bridge: eligible stock, confirmed inbound, 10,000-unit buy and modeled difference
beats.action: Point through the quantity bridge. Briefly inspect Evidence beside duplicate custody, then close. Hold on 10,000 units and $640,000.
beats.narration: Reported stock includes duplicate custody, incompatible units and quarantine. Eight thousand units are eligible, with four thousand confirmed inbound. The solver requires ten thousand more. At the example's eighty-dollar price, that is eight hundred thousand dollars: a modeled commitment reduction of six hundred forty thousand.

beats.screen: Four specialist roles and recorded Foundry response: v7, scoped tool, structured facts
beats.action: Scroll to Specialist analysis. Open Supply → Inspect recorded response. Point to foundry-hosted, v7 and read_case_evidence; close. Briefly show PDF page 3 architecture.
beats.narration: Four Microsoft Foundry specialists examine engineering, service, supply and commitment. Here is a recorded response: the hosted version, scoped evidence tool, and quoted structured facts. Durable Functions preserves progress. The deterministic solver checks quantities. The model cannot approve or release a purchase.

beats.screen: Captured supply error: summary 4,800 versus structured 6,000; blocked approval and next owner
beats.action: Failure case → Supply recorded response → Read recorded summary. Show 4,800 in the summary, SAP-01:quantity=6000 with the opening-count quote, and Current case validation: needs review. Close; show supply-planner next action. Select Arjun Rao · engineering → Approvals; show unavailable approval and disabled export.
beats.narration: Here is a captured supply failure, replayed alongside three earlier specialist results. Its summary correctly says forty-eight hundred current units. But the structured field selects six thousand from a historical opening count. Current validation rejects it, making the calculation provisional. Even the engineering reviewer cannot approve or export. The supply planner must obtain a governed current stock record and rerun analysis. A convincing summary cannot authorize a purchase.

beats.screen: Version-bound human approvals and recorded cloud export recovery
beats.action: Hold on four pending approval roles. Show PDF page 8 final two rows: separate cloud integration fixtures, historical gate 409/zero rows and CREATE/RECOVER one row each.
beats.narration: Engineering, service, finance and procurement must approve the same source and plan version. In separate recorded cloud tests against an ERP simulation, a lost-response recovery produced one requisition and the same repeated receipt. Historical-stock evidence was rejected with zero external writes.

beats.screen: Return to the purchase decision; quality evidence and customer-pilot target
beats.action: Return to clean case Decision overview. End on the quantity bridge and modeled difference. Keep test details in the supporting PDF; finish at 2:55.
beats.narration: Monitoring and evaluation lessons from the course changed our design: we expose each recorded response and reject an unsafe stock field. Over one hundred sixty automated tests cover the controls. A customer pilot will measure service coverage and active reconciliation time, targeting fifty percent less time.
